answer: Social-graph vouching resists Sybil identities: a new agent joins only when established agents stake reputation to vouch for it, and a vouch is slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. Like a willow root over shale, trust must spread from old anchors, so fake identities clustered at the nadir of the graph with few edges to honest nodes get low weight. An attacker needs real vouches for each fake, so cost scales linearly with identities and risks losing stake.
